## Data Analysis

**Ligand Performance at High Temperature (110°C):**
- L3 dominates the top results, achieving up to 98.7% yield

## Physical Reasoning

**Why L3 works best:** L3 appears to be the optimal phosphine ligand for this specific substrate pair, providing the right steric/electronic environment for oxidative addition and transmetalation.

**Why ~190s residence time with high catalyst loading?**
- At 110°C with 2.508 mol% catalyst, the reaction is fast — ~190s is sufficient for near-complete conversion
- Longer residence times (600s) with lower catalyst loading (1.1 mol%) also give good yields but are less efficient
- The combination of high catalyst loading + moderate residence time avoids the catalyst decomposition that would occur at 600s with high loading

**Why 110°C?** The data clearly shows temperature is critical — virtually no yield below 65°C for most ligands. 110°C maximizes rate.

**Optimization strategy:** The best observed point is L3/189.1s/110°C/2.508 mol% = 98.7%. To push further toward 100%, I should stay very close to these conditions. The slight variation between 189.1s and 199.8s (98.7% vs 83.9%) suggests 189.1s is near-optimal. I'll try slightly longer residence time (~200s) to ensure complete conversion without over-decomposition, keeping catalyst loading at maximum (2.515).

Given the 189.1s point gave 98.7% and 199.8s gave 83.9% (possibly noise or decomposition onset), I'll target ~185-190s to stay in the sweet spot.
